cases.notes: Replaces ltx2_twostage_t2v and ltx2.3_twostage_t2v_2gpus (retired 2026-10-24); their published results stay in the reports. The workload is LTX-2.5's official distilled two-stage recipe, which is the model's default path: model_index.json points at the distilled DiT (transformer/), whose weights are distilled themselves, so both stages run the same checkpoint and no stage swaps in a LoRA. Stage 1 runs at half resolution (960x544) over the 8 distilled sigmas, the latents go through the x2 latent upsampler, and stage 2 refines at 1920x1088 over the 3-sigma tail (0.909375, 0.725, 0.421875): 8 + 3 DiT forwards, unguided (CFG 1, STG and modality guidance off), so there is no negative prompt and no CFG branch. Sources: the Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers model card ('Two-stage distilled generation': stage 1 544x960, 121 frames, 24 fps, DISTILLED_SIGMA_VALUES, then STAGE_2_DISTILLED_SIGMA_VALUES at 2x), sglang's LTX-2.5 cookbook (LTX2TwoStagePipeline at 1920x1088, the distilled DiT runs a pinned 8-sigma schedule, CFG parallelism does not apply), and vLLM-Omni's recipe (LTX2DistilledTwoStagePipeline, 1920x1088, 8 + 3 steps). ltx-pipelines' distilled CLI defaults to 1536x1024 with the same schedule. Not a reduced-step substitute: every framework runs the same weights, schedule, guidance, size, frames and fps. Audio is on (joint video + audio, 48 kHz vocoder) and the video decodes with the convolutional VAE (vae/); the optional diffusion decoder and duration head stay off. The conv VAE is the default of diffusers' LTX2Pipeline and of sglang; ltx-pipelines, vLLM-Omni and LightX2V decode with the diffusion VAE by default, so vLLM-Omni is pinned to the conv VAE through its documented ltx2_use_conv_vae switch. Stage 1's sampler differs in kind: ltx-pipelines, vLLM-Omni, FastVideo and ComfyUI step stage 1 with an ancestral Euler (fresh noise each step), diffusers and sglang with plain Euler; the cost is one noise draw per step on a 960x544 latent. Prompt and seed are the retired LTX rows' (the model card asks for long captions; the text encoder pads to a fixed length either way).
